newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - June 17.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - June 17.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Tuesday:

* In the U.S market, blue-chip stocks fell on Monday, ending a string of six record closing highs, but the broader market continued its rally. The Dow Jones Industrial Average ended down 9.95 points at 7,772.09 on Monday, slipping below Friday's record finish of 7,782.04.
* Indonesia's central bank reported that Indonesia's offshore debts were US$109.3 billion as of last March, while foreign exchange reserves increased to $19.9 billion.

* On Monday, the Jakarta composite index ended up 6.67 points, or 0.95 percent, at 705.29 points in active trading on foreign-led buying following Friday's sharp gains on Wall Street and recent announcements of upward revisions in 1997 net profit forecasts, brokers said.
* On Tuesday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,428.00/29.00 at 0130 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,427.50/28.50.

* Bacelius Ruru, director general of the state-owned companies supervisory body, reportedly said the planned merger of state banks would be completed before Asean Free Trade Area (AFTA) is reached in 2003. The report could help sentiment towards Bank Negara Indonesia.

* Property firm PT Surya Semesta Internusa on a report that the firm was planning to set up a joint venture with an Australian-based firm. Also following market talk Semesta was holding talks with a firm controlled by a conglomerate to develop a container harbour in its industrial park.

* Bank BDNI on a report that its first quarter net profit was 69.1 billion rupiah, compared with 39.2 billion rupiah in the same 1996 period. The bank expected to book net profit of 350 billion rupiah for 1997, compared with 190 billion rupiah in 1996.

* Pulp and paper maker Indah Kiat Pulp and Paper on a report in Bisnis Indonesia that it will change its plan to use the proceeds of a proposed rights issue. Previously it said the proceeds would be used to establish a 10th pulp mill. The paper did not provide details.
* Textile company Argo Pantes on a report that it saw net profit of 30 billion rupiah for 1997.

* Plantation firm PT London Sumatra on a report in Bisnis Indonesia that it projected its total palm plantation would be about 45,032 hectares by March 1998, while it had developed about 21,650 hectares by May 1997.
* Toll road operator Citra Marga Nusaphala ahead of its shareholders' meeting on Tuesday afternoon.
* Bank Papan Sejahtera following reports that the Indonesian central bank will divest its 13.11 percent stake in the bank.
